static_traits.name: Lin Yucheng
static_traits.social_status: Has one supportive friend, but is unwilling to discuss career dissatisfaction with them; mood changes and declining enthusiasm affect interactions with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of similar psychological problems; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, highly cooperative; able to identify and describe their own thought patterns and emotional effects; positive attitude, willing to try reframing and exercises

basic_info.main_problem: I often feel I should be doing more in my career, especially given my experience writing romance novels under a pen name and hiking the Appalachian Trail. This mindset leads to dissatisfaction and self-doubt.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of dissatisfaction affect my mood and drive, making it hard to enjoy my interests and work, so I am seeking counseling to shift perspective, ease dissatisfaction, and boost motivation.
growth_experiences: For a long time has been writing romance novels under a pen name, taking writing as an important interest and commitment, which strengthens the expectation of writing as a potential career direction.
Completing the Appalachian Trail hike reinforced longing for a 'more adventurous lifestyle', contrasting with current work.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on professional success and achievement

special_situations.event: At the moment of getting off work after a whole day of heavy work, physically and mentally exhausted
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not yet a successful writer or living a more adventurous life, it means I failed and am wasting time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Through setting more aggressive career goals and proactively expanding my network, I 'prove myself'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I'll never become a writer / I shouldn't waste time on this job

special_situations.event: When seeing or thinking of peers/others succeeding in a writing career or having a more adventurous lifestyle
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fall short of others, it means I am not good enough and worth less
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequent social comparison, reinforcing self-demands to close the gap
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am falling behind

special_situations.event: Realizing current work doesn't match passions like writing/hiking
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If work doesn't align with passion, then the job is meaningless and utterly worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating the positive aspects of current work, pushing myself to transition quickly

special_situations.event: Still no clear progress after setting transition goals and networking for a while
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If no results are visible short-term, it means I can't do it and the future won't change
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further intensifies self-criticism and 'should' self-demands, increasing pressure to force change
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It seems nothing will ever change; I'll be stuck here forever

core_conflict.wish: Longs for a life consistent with inner passion and recognized (becoming a more successful creator / a more adventurous person)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and appearing inferior in comparison, being judged as not good enough and wasting life
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control and drive through strict 'shoulds' and social comparison, avoiding facing failure and unworthiness

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough chaser lagging behind others
object_relations.object_representation: Others/society with harsh evaluation standards, constantly comparing and scrutinizing

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to focus more deeply on inner emotions and sense of self-worth (rather than goals or techniques)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to understand the problem as a 'task' needing more planning and action, rather than an emotional and values conflict (turning emotional distress into a rational task)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Discuss plans and steps in an objective, analytical tone, reducing emotional vocabulary, emphasizing goals and efficiency, downplaying vulnerability and unease.

manifestations: Strongly feeling that current work doesn't align with inner passion after work, believing 'this job is meaningless'
When comparing with others' success and adventurous lives, the hollow sense of worth intensifies
outcomes: Decreased drive, struggling to enjoy writing and hiking

manifestations: Having a supportive friend but unwilling to discuss career dissatisfaction, reducing connection and support
outcomes: Insufficient emotional support, prone to harsh self-criticism under stress

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should' statements to demand more from myself in my career
Using society's/others' success as an internal judgment standard, ignoring one's own pace and circumstances

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Focusing attention on self-doubt and falling behind, reinforcing harsh self-criticism
Keeping career dissatisfaction from friends, unwilling to express needs, reducing opportunities for support

positive_force: Positive attitude, actively seeking counseling and change
Has clear interests and past achievements (writing, hiking) that can serve as resources
Able to identify and reframe negative thinking, willing to practice affirmations and visualization
Good work performance, with stability and a basic sense of efficacy
Has one supportive friend who could potentially offer emotional and practical support
negative_force: Overusing 'should' and overgeneralizing, forming a cycle of harsh self-criticism
Frequent social comparison, ignoring own progress and circumstances, reinforcing inferiority
Negating the positive aspects and transitional value of current work (disqualifying the positive)
Unwilling to discuss troubles with friends, underutilized support system
Emotional and physical exhaustion after work, triggering negative automatic thoughts

target_behavior.behavior: Career-related self-reproach and negative automatic thoughts ('should' statements, overgeneralization, and comparison)
antecedent: Physically and mentally exhausted after work
Sees or thinks of others' success in writing or adventurous living
No clear progress yet after setting goals and networking
target_behavior.core_reason: Core belief 'I am not good enough', tightly binding self-worth to achievement, and introjecting social standards into rigid 'should' rules
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control and driving change through self-whipping, while avoiding facing the vulnerability of failure and worthlessness
target_behavior.consequence: Dissatisfaction and increased stress, decreased drive, struggling to enjoy writing and hiking; interpersonal relationships affected
